Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"

// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "853baab97b1f3b03c1ffa55797e87867f5fb7ce33457411f56afd270cb395453", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "41acb30b9d662d48b7b4fc0ac3d4b79f") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "853baab97b1f3b03c1ffa55797e87867f5fb7ce33457411f56afd270cb395453", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "41acb30b9d662d48b7b4fc0ac3d4b79f") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "853baab97b1f3b03c1ffa55797e87867f5fb7ce33457411f56afd270cb395453", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "41acb30b9d662d48b7b4fc0ac3d4b79f")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "853baab97b1f3b03c1ffa55797e87867f5fb7ce33457411f56afd270cb395453", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "41acb30b9d662d48b7b4fc0ac3d4b79f") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "853baab97b1f3b03c1ffa55797e87867f5fb7ce33457411f56afd270cb395453", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "41acb30b9d662d48b7b4fc0ac3d4b79f") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "853baab97b1f3b03c1ffa55797e87867f5fb7ce33457411f56afd270cb395453", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "41acb30b9d662d48b7b4fc0ac3d4b79f")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "853baab97b1f3b03c1ffa55797e87867f5fb7ce33457411f56afd270cb395453", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "41acb30b9d662d48b7b4fc0ac3d4b79f"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Unauthenticated write/read to mcp-memory-service /api/documents/* endpoints (CVE-2026-50027) AIExploitation High
Hunts HTTP 200 responses to the unauthenticated document-API routes (upload, batch-upload, search-content, history) on a mcp-memory-service HTTP server, where the request carried no Authorization header. This is the confidentiality/integrity half of the auth-bypass: memory poisoning via upload and stored-content disclosure via search-content/history. Rationale: Anchored on the exact vulnerable route prefixes named at documents.py source lines (upload:149, search-content:729, history) plus HTTP 200; ImWebSession's HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization lets us assert the request was truly unauthenticated, which is the article's core inconsistency (/api/memories 401 vs /api/documents 200). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-84hp-mqvj-3p8h • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/mcp-memory-service/CVE-2026-50027/
ATT&CKT1190 T1213 T1565.001
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Operator deployed the HTTP server WITHOUT MCP_API_KEY/OAuth enabled, so legitimate clients also send no Authorization header
  • Internal ingestion/backup automation that bulk-uploads documents via the same API
  • Vulnerability scanners (Nessus/Nuclei) probing the documented CVE route
  • The operator's own PoC/pen-test traffic against 127.0.0.1
  • Health-check or uptime probes hitting /api/documents/history
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !startswith "127." and SrcIpAddr != "::1"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull all SrcIpAddr hitting /api/documents/* with empty Authorization; confirm the server was launched with MCP_API_KEY/OAuth set (grep env of the memory server --http process). If auth was enabled, every unauthenticated 200 is a real bypass. 2) CONTAIN: Put the service behind the reverse proxy's auth or a WAF rule denying /api/documents/* without a valid bearer, and upgrade mcp-memory-service to >=10.67.1. 3) HUNT: For each attacker IP, correlate preceding /api/memories 401s and following DELETE /api/documents/remove-by-tags; review search-content/{upload_id} responses for exfiltrated memory content and inspect newly uploaded documents for prompt-injection payloads.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Url has "/api/documents/"
| where Url has_any ("/upload", "/batch-upload", "/search-content/", "/history")
| where HttpStatusCode == 200
| where isempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization)   // no API key / OAuth bearer supplied = the CVE-2026-50027 bypass
| where SrcIpAddr !startswith "127."
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

mcp-memory-service auth-bypass fingerprint: /api/memories 401 then /api/documents 200 from same source AIExploitation High
Correlates the CVE-2026-50027 PoC signature on a single source IP: a 401 on the correctly-protected /api/memories endpoint followed within the hour by a successful (200) request to a /api/documents/* route with no credentials. This two-event shape is far higher fidelity than either request alone because it captures an attacker discovering the inconsistent auth boundary and pivoting to the unprotected router. Rationale: Directly models the PoC attack chain (STEP 1 GET /api/memories -> 401, STEP 4/5 POST/DELETE /api/documents/* -> 200) as a same-source temporal correlation; the 401-then-200 pairing is the article's own proof that the attacker found and exploited the inconsistent auth boundary, making it very low FP. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-84hp-mqvj-3p8h • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/mcp-memory-service/CVE-2026-50027/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A misconfigured legitimate client whose token expired (401 on /api/memories) while a separate unauthenticated automation happens to hit /api/documents from the same NAT egress IP
  • Security scanner walking every route and recording both a 401 and a 200 from one host
  • Shared corporate proxy/NAT collapsing many users behind one SrcIpAddr
  • Operator testing both endpoints during troubleshooting
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the source IP is not a known internal proxy/scanner; inspect the exact /api/documents route that returned 200 (upload = poisoning, search-content = read, remove* = destruction). 2) CONTAIN: Block the source at the WAF/reverse proxy, disable the /api/documents/* router or gate it behind auth, and upgrade to mcp-memory-service >=10.67.1. 3) HUNT: Enumerate every upload_id this IP created or deleted; snapshot current memory store contents, diff against last known-good backup, and purge attacker-injected documents to prevent downstream prompt-injection of the AI agent.
let window = 1h;
let probes = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
    | where Url has "/api/memories" and HttpStatusCode == 401
    | project ProbeTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Url has "/api/documents/" and HttpStatusCode == 200
| where isempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization)
| join kind=inner probes on SrcIpAddr
| where TimeGenerated between (ProbeTime .. ProbeTime + window)
| project ProbeTime, BypassTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod, Url
| order by BypassTime desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/api/memories*" OR Web.url="*/api/documents/*") by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.status, _time span=5m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| eval memories_401=if(like(url,"%/api/memories%") AND status=401, count, 0)
| eval docs_bypass=if(like(url,"%/api/documents/%") AND status=200, count, 0)
| stats sum(memories_401) as memories_401, sum(docs_bypass) as docs_bypass, values(url) as urls, values(dest) as dest, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime by src
| where memories_401 > 0 AND docs_bypass > 0
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime

Unauthenticated mass memory deletion via mcp-memory-service DELETE /api/documents/remove-by-tags AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts successful (200) DELETE requests to the unauthenticated /api/documents/remove-by-tags and /api/documents/remove/{upload_id} routes — the availability/integrity impact of CVE-2026-50027 where an attacker permanently destroys memories belonging to authenticated users without credentials. A burst of such DELETEs from one source is a destruction event. Rationale: Uses the specific destructive routes and sink named in the article (remove-by-tags -> storage.delete_by_tags at line 705, remove/{upload_id}) constrained to DELETE + 200; a successful unauthenticated DELETE to these paths is by definition the CVE's availability impact (STEP 5 memories_deleted=1) with essentially no benign equivalent when auth is enabled. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-84hp-mqvj-3p8h • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/mcp-memory-service/CVE-2026-50027/
ATT&CKT1485 T1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin housekeeping that prunes documents by tag through the same API
  • Automated retention/cleanup job deleting expired memories
  • Operator running the published PoC (tag cve-poc) during validation
  • Server started without MCP_API_KEY so all DELETEs are legitimately unauthenticated
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !startswith "127." and SrcIpAddr != "::1"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the DELETEs are unauthenticated (empty Authorization) and the server was configured with auth; count how many upload_ids/tags were removed and from which SrcIpAddr. 2) CONTAIN: Immediately block the source, take the HTTP server offline or gate /api/documents/* behind auth, upgrade to >=10.67.1, and freeze the storage backend for forensic capture before it is overwritten. 3) HUNT: Restore deleted memories from the most recent backup, diff to quantify loss, and pivot on the same IP for prior upload (poisoning) and search-content (exfiltration) calls to scope the full read/write/delete blast radius.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where HttpMethod == "DELETE"
| where Url has_any ("/api/documents/remove-by-tags", "/api/documents/remove/")
| where HttpStatusCode == 200
| where isempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization)
| summarize DeleteCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Urls = make_set(Url, 20) by SrcIpAddr, DstHostname
| order by DeleteCount desc

// Article-specific bespoke detection — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-50027: mcp-memory-service: Missing Authentication on
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("documents.py", "memories.py", "run_server.py", "poc.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/tmp/poc.txt", "/root/.cache/huggingface", "/var/lib/apt/lists/", "/usr/bin/env") or FileName in~ ("documents.py", "memories.py", "run_server.py", "poc.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Article-specific bespoke detection — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-50027: mcp-memory-service: Missing Authentication on ```
| tstats `summariesonly` count earliest(_time) AS firstTime latest(_time) AS lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process_name IN ("documents.py","memories.py","run_server.py","poc.py"))
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name,
       Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| append [
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified")
      AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/poc.txt*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/root/.cache/huggingface*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/lib/apt/lists/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/usr/bin/env*" OR Filesystem.file_name IN ("documents.py","memories.py","run_server.py","poc.py"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]
